# kilo — fleet context integration

**Layer:** `mcp`  ·  **Status:** `planned`  ·  **Surface:** `~/.config/kilo/kilo.json [mcp.<name>] (or `kilo mcp add`)`

This harness reads MCP servers from its own configuration, so its TOOL surface needs **no shim** — registration is a config entry. (MCP has no lifecycle, so a harness may still ship a small trigger artifact; see *Shipped artifact*.)

## Why this layer

Kilo Code CLI is MCP-native: MCP servers live under the top-level `mcp`
key of ~/.config/kilo/kilo.json (global; also supports kilo.jsonc /
config.json; project-scope: ./kilo.json or ./.kilo/kilo.json, project
takes precedence). It is a fork of OpenCode — the same `type: local` +
`command` ARRAY shape (NOT a string, so this entry is a sibling of the
opencode one, never a copy of the Claude/Codex one). Declared from Kilo's
own MCP docs (read 2026-11-25):
https://kilo.ai/docs/automate/mcp/using-in-cli and
https://kilo.ai/docs/automate/mcp/using-in-kilo-code. `kilo mcp list` is
the read-back (presence `cmd:kilo` is the installed CLI, measured as
kilo 7.8.32 on this host).

OWED BEFORE `documented`: which env var carries the harness's session id
into the MCP child is UNVERIFIED (see the per-harness table in the
cross-agent-design skill). If none reaches the child the resolver answers
"per-repo, shared" — a real defect for lock ownership, not a cosmetic one.

## Install

```bash
# provider + model: `kilo auth` (or /connect in the TUI); provider, model,
# permission and MCP settings all live in ~/.config/kilo/kilo.json
Add to ~/.config/kilo/kilo.json:
  { "mcp": { "fleet-context": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["<fleet venv python>", "<mcp_server>"] } } }
# read back:  kilo mcp list
```

## Verify (do not report a wiring you have not exercised)

1. kilo mcp list shows fleet-context.
2. In a Kilo session call mem_context — the peer card must come back.
3. Session identity (which env var reaches the MCP child) is UNVERIFIED for Kilo — resolve it before promoting this entry.

## Session identity

One session = one identity. Precedence is identical in every layer (args → env → git), which is what lets a checkpoint written here be restored by another harness.

```bash
export FLEET_SESSION_HARNESS=<value>
export FLEET_SESSION_REPO=<value>
export FLEET_SESSION_BRANCH=<value>
```

Overrides (usually unnecessary, needed on macOS):

```bash
export FLEET_CONTEXT_CLI=<path>   # see the failure modes in the runbook
export FLEET_CONTEXT_PYTHON=<path>   # see the failure modes in the runbook
```

- MCP server: `~/steadfaste-fleet/mcp-servers/fleet-context-mcp.py`
